minutes.headline: Assessors aim to finish abatement reviews by June 15, defer to the valuation firm, and went into executive session.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors opened with a statement on the abatement process and appeals. They said they would defer to the outside valuation firm on property values and point disputed values to the Appellate Tax Board. They set remote work sessions to finish abatements in time for tax bills, answered a resident's question about notification mailings, then voted to enter executive session.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors said questions about particular property values will go to the outside valuation firm, and the board will follow the firm if it does not agree with a change.
The board set remote work sessions to finish abatements: one the next day at two o'clock and one Thursday, June 15, at three o'clock, with another the following week if needed.
The board opened with a statement on the abatement process and the Appellate Tax Board appeal window, and pointed disputed values to that board.
A resident asked whether the board is on schedule to finish abatements by the 15th.
A resident asked whether notifications to residents were still behind, and the board then moved into executive session. No votes were recorded.

why_it_matters: A homeowner who disagrees with an assessed value has a review by the valuation firm first, and the Appellate Tax Board as the next step, so the appeal window in the board's opening statement is the deadline to watch.
Abatement decisions are being finished against the date tax bills go out, and residents who say they received no notification may not know where their own abatement stands.
